sources.entry: remark42 - Lightweight and simple comment engine, which doesn't spy on users. It can be embedded into blogs, articles or any other place where readers add comments. (Demo, Source Code) MIT Docker/Go

summary.one_liner: Remark42 is a self-hosted, lightweight comment engine for blogs and articles that its authors describe as not spying on users.
summary.what_it_does: Remark42 is a self-hosted comment system that can be embedded into blogs, articles, or any other page where readers leave comments. It supports social login through Google, Facebook, Microsoft, GitHub, Apple, Yandex, Patreon, Discord, Telegram and custom OAuth2 providers, plus email login and optional anonymous access. Comments can be nested multiple levels deep and shown as a tree or as a plain list, with Markdown support, image upload by drag-and-drop, voting, pinning, and sorting. Moderators can remove comments and block users. Data is stored in a single embedded data file rather than an external database, with JSON export and automatic backups. Admins can be notified of new comments via Telegram, Slack, webhook, or email, and users can get email or Telegram replies.
use_cases: add comments to a personal blog
replace Disqus with a private alternative
how_to_run: Deploy with Docker (README states it is fully dockerized and can be deployed in a single command)
Or download the self-contained executable for Linux, Windows or macOS
See the project's documentation for configuration details
notable: Embedded single data file storage, no external database needed
Social login with many providers plus email and anonymous access
Imports comments from Disqus and WordPress
Multi-site mode from a single instance
Privacy focused, does not spy on users
caveats: Admin and contribution details are only linked from the README, not described inline
Setup beyond the single-command Docker deployment is not detailed in the README
